Understand user patterns and find silent failures in your AI agents.

The Context Company helps teams analyze AI agent conversations to surface user behavior patterns, performance trends, and moments where agents struggle - so teams know what’s working, what’s not, and what to improve next.

long_description.after:
We analyze every conversation between your customers and your AI agent to find what's losing you customers and money. Then we help ship the fix and prove it worked.

Nobody on the team can read every conversation once an agent is in production. TCC does, and turns them into patterns tied to the accounts they affect: where customers get stuck, what they wish the agent could do, and where it's spending more than it needs to.

Engineers ask about a pattern from their IDE through our MCP, get the conversations and traces behind it down to the tool call or prompt that went wrong, ship the fix, and benchmark cost and quality before and after. Product sees what customers are actually trying to do with the agent and where it falls short, broken out by topic and account, which becomes the backlog for what to build next. Customer success sees which accounts the agent is struggling with before the customer says anything, and steps in with the full conversation on hand.

Any agent framework, a few lines of code. If you're running an agent in production or about to launch, ping us.

Skillsync is local-first and yours, and its core engine, txcript, is open source, a portable session format that no single provider owns.

long_description.before:
Audio-visual translation infrastructure for all video, live and recorded -- the first and only that works in real time. World translation: not just changing voice and lips into a new language, but understanding the scene, the sound, and preserving the human.

🦋 Movies & TV, Micro-dramas, Live Broadcasts, Live Shopping, Corporate & Education, Ads, Creators & Podcasts, Platforms. Day-and-date, in every territory.

Founders An Zhu Liu, Jibin Song, Mingi Kwon, and Xu Zheng lead a team of PhDs, professors, and researchers from the world's top universities who started the field of joint audio-visual human models and co-authored the current state of the art in real-time human animation. Since 2021: over 10,000 citations and 100+ papers at ICLR, NeurIPS, CVPR, ECCV, and more.

Translation needs 3D world understanding, permanence of identities. A translator has to know who's speaking: where every sound in the dense polyphony originates (laughter, layered crowds). Laughter here, a short yell there, a voice from off-screen, someone on screen mouthing words before being interrupted. Everyone else scaffolds separate models and pre-processing; a unified model simulates the scene. It's a spatio-temporal reasoner: predicting continuity across frames forces it to internalize 3D geometry, spatial reasoning, and permanence -- of objects, people, and the environment itself. The scene state survives the edit: when the shot pans or cuts away, someone off-screen still exists, still owns their voice, and is still there when the camera comes back. Multiple people, side views, off angles, dense polyphony, fast motion -- the hard cases hold.

Vs ElevenLabs: they lose the laughter, the music, the ambiance -- 270% more background-sound error -- and ours sounds 27.8% more like you. That means no recasting, no ADR, no M&E stems required -- it works from the final mix.

Vs human translators: 100.3% of their quality -- scalable, real time. Published benchmarks: https://thefamiliarlab.com/benchmark

long_description.before:
CarSignal is the AI-native operating system for independent auto repair shops.

Most shops still run each repair across disconnected management software, scan tools, parts catalogs, service information, texts, spreadsheets, and knowledge kept in technicians’ heads. That fragmentation slows diagnosis, creates duplicate admin, and leaves customers waiting.

CarSignal connects the full repair process in one system. AI agents research vehicle-specific failure patterns and surface the tests that confirm or rule out each cause. The same system carries each job from booking and intake through inspections, estimates, parts, approvals, payment, and follow-up, so technicians spend less time searching and updating systems and more time fixing cars.

long_description.before:
Decawork gives IT teams one place to deploy, govern and maintain the AI agents running across their company.

Building internal AI tools and agents is getting easier. Turning them into company-owned systems is still hard. What follows is agent sprawl: deployment gets messy, agents go live with access to real systems and real data, and maintenance falls in the gap. IT can't see any of it, so it does the only two things it can: first ignore, then block. Ignoring piles up risk; blocking kills the productivity people just found. 

With Decawork, every agent ships one standard way: its own identity and scoped credentials, with IT's sign-off before it goes live. After that, every run is watched - IT is alerted the moment something fails, agents nobody uses get retired. And the whole time, IT sees every agent, controls what it can touch, and audits every action, with approvals gating anything sensitive.

Every big shift - cloud, SaaS, the digital workspace - ended with IT running it. Agents aren't just the next shift, they're the next workforce, bigger than the human one. Decawork is what IT will run them with.
long_description.after:
Decawork is building AI models that control what agents do inside companies.

Giving an agent access to a system does not tell it when using that access is right for the business. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. IT teams understand the business, but they can’t turn every judgment into a rule or manually approve every step.

We train individual models for companies that understand its business, critical systems, and priorities. It learns from the policies IT teams set and the decisions they make in practice. We’re training these models to combine that understanding with an agent’s task and past actions to decide what it should be allowed to do in real time.

Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. And Decawork is building those models.

one_liner.after: AI models that control AI agents inside your company.
